cases.purpose: --partx-kernel add with MIN/MAX ranges issues BLKPG_ADD_PARTITION per selected table entry on a loop device so sysfs start/size match the DOS table written by sfdisk; delete removes a range; add with no bounds adds every used entry.
cases.oracle: Kernel partition set read from sysfs (start/size in sectors per loopNpM), compared with the table written independently by util-linux sfdisk or requested from fdisk (--create-mbr specs); BLKPG semantics per partx(8)/blkpg ioctl.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.
cases.script:
. ./rl.sh
kp() { local p s z o=; for p in /sys/block/$LN/${LN}p*; do [[ -e $p ]] || continue; read -r s < $p/start; read -r z < $p/size; o+=" p${p##*p}=$s+$z"; done; echo "  kernel:${o:- none}"; }
f() { local l=$1; shift; fdisk "$@" >o.txt 2>&1; local rc=$?; local m; m=$(norm o.txt | /usr/bin/sed 's/^.*fdisk: //' | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'); printf '%s status=%s msg=[%s]\n' "$l" $rc "$m"; }
tbl() { /usr/bin/truncate -s 8M disk.img; at disk.img; L=$REPLY; LN=${L#/dev/}; reg $L LOOP; }
mbr3() { /usr/sbin/sfdisk -q disk.img <<E
label: dos
label-id: 0x12345678
start=2048, size=2048, type=83
start=4096, size=4096, type=83
start=8192, size=${1:-2048}, type=83
E
}
tbl; mbr3
kp
f add-2-2 --partx-kernel add $L 2 2; kp
f add-3-3 --partx-kernel add $L 3 3; kp
f add-1 --partx-kernel add $L 1 1; kp
f delete-1-3 --partx-kernel delete $L 1 3; kp
f add-all --partx-kernel add $L; kp
cases.stdout:
kernel: none
add-2-2 status=0 msg=[BLKPG add applied to 1 partition(s) on LOOP|]
  kernel: p2=4096+4096
add-3-3 status=0 msg=[BLKPG add applied to 1 partition(s) on LOOP|]
  kernel: p2=4096+4096 p3=8192+2048
add-1 status=0 msg=[BLKPG add applied to 1 partition(s) on LOOP|]
  kernel: p1=2048+2048 p2=4096+4096 p3=8192+2048
delete-1-3 status=0 msg=[BLKPG delete applied to 3 partition(s) on LOOP|]
  kernel: none
add-all status=0 msg=[BLKPG add applied to 3 partition(s) on LOOP|]
  kernel: p1=2048+2048 p2=4096+4096 p3=8192+2048

cases.purpose: After --create-mbr on a partscan loop device the kernel partition set follows the new table (also when shrinking); with a partition mounted the reread fails with a BLKRRPART warning (EBUSY), the on-disk table is still updated and the kernel set stays unchanged; after umount a rewrite is reread cleanly.
cases.oracle: Kernel partition set read from sysfs (start/size in sectors per loopNpM), compared with the table written independently by util-linux sfdisk or requested from fdisk (--create-mbr specs); BLKPG semantics per partx(8)/blkpg ioctl.

. ./rl.sh
kp() { local p s z o=; for p in /sys/block/$LN/${LN}p*; do [[ -e $p ]] || continue; read -r s < $p/start; read -r z < $p/size; o+=" p${p##*p}=$s+$z"; done; echo "  kernel:${o:- none}"; }

start=2048, size=2048, type=83
start=4096, size=4096, type=83
start=8192, size=${1:-2048}, type=83
E
}
tbl
mk() { fdisk --create-mbr $L "$@" >o.txt 2>&1; local rc=$?; local w=no; [[ $(< o.txt) == *"BLKRRPART warning"* ]] && w=yes; printf '%s status=%s rrpart-warning=%s\n' "$LBL" $rc $w; }
LBL=write-two; mk 2048,2048 4096,4096; kp
LBL=shrink-to-one; mk 2048,2048; kp
$MK -q -t ext2 ${L}p1; /usr/bin/mkdir -p mnt; /usr/bin/mount ${L}p1 mnt
LBL=write-while-mounted; mk 2048,2048 4096,2048; kp
echo "  disk:$(/usr/sbin/sfdisk -d disk.img | /usr/bin/grep -c 'start=')-partitions p2=$(/usr/sbin/sfdisk -d disk.img | /usr/bin/sed -n 's/.*disk.img2 *: *start= *\([0-9]*\), size= *\([0-9]*\).*/\1+\2/p')"
/usr/bin/umount mnt
LBL=write-after-umount; mk 2048,2048 4096,2048; kp
cases.stdout:
write-two status=0 rrpart-warning=no
  kernel: p1=2048+2048 p2=4096+4096
shrink-to-one status=0 rrpart-warning=no
  kernel: p1=2048+2048
write-while-mounted status=0 rrpart-warning=yes
  kernel: p1=2048+2048
  disk:2-partitions p2=4096+2048
write-after-umount status=0 rrpart-warning=no
  kernel: p1=2048+2048 p2=4096+2048
